methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $100M total raised proxy.

private.name: Cuby Technologies

data.narrative:
Cover is a Series B-stage housing and construction company founded by Alexis Rivas and Jemuel Joseph. The company has raised over $100M to date. The comparable universe for this sector is limited, with only one identified private peer (Cuby Technologies) and no public comparables, reflecting the nascent nature of frontier-tech construction businesses.

Valuation analysis relies on a stage-progression methodology, which is applicable given Cover's defined Series B stage and known capital raise history. Using the $100M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a typical Series B-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $190M. This single-method approach generates a triangulated range with a median of $190M, a low-end estimate of $162M (approximately 15% discount), and a high-end estimate of $218M (approximately 15% premium).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M to $218M, with $190M as the central point estimate. Key uncertainties include the limited comparables universe—reliance on a single private peer and absence of public company benchmarks—and dependence on stage-progression multipliers, which may not fully capture sector-specific growth dynamics or Cover's differentiated positioning. A more granular valuation would benefit from revenue run-rate, margin structure, and customer concentration data.
